question: The managing authority for the Just Transition Fund is responsible for forwarding cumulative data, the values of output and result indicators, and financial instrument data for the 2021-2027 Just Transition Fund to the Commission, in accordance with Article 42 of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060.

This data must be submitted by 31 January, 30 April, 31 July, 30 September and 30 November of each year and reflect the situation on the last day of the previous month. Article 69 of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 states that the Member States must ensure that the managing authorities provide regular forecasts of the amount for interim payment applications.

These forecasts must be submitted by 31 January and 31 July of each year, in accordance with Annex VIII to the regulation. The data for November 2023 and January 2024 has not been published on the Just Transition Fund website for Taranto and Sulcis Iglesiente1.
In view of the above, can the Commission say whether Italy met the data submission deadlines laid down in Articles 42 and 69 of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 in respect of 2023 and 2024?
answer: According to Article 42 of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 (2), Italy transmitted, for the Just Transition Fund national programme, cumulative data on number of selected operations, their total eligible cost, the contribution from the Funds and the total eligible expenditure declared by the beneficiaries on 13 September 2023 (also including values of output and result indicators for selected operations and values achieved by operations), on 2 October 2023 and on 28 November 2023.

The cumulative data required by 31 January 2024 and by 30 April 2024 were not transmitted to the Commission. As per Article 69(10) of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060, payment forecasts were transmitted on 31 January 2023 and 1 August 2023. No payment forecasts were transmitted for 2024.

The Commission solicited multiple times Italian authorities responsible for the Just Transition Fund national programme to ensure regulatory requirements are respected, including the timely transmission of data and payment forecasts.
